FN-PI1PGE-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 8
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Representative Randy Wood
Security
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 03/20/2023
House Bill 8 as introduced could increase the obligations of state and local law enforcement
agencies by an undetermined amount related to the record keeping and reporting of traffic stops
made under the provisions of this bill. This bill would also increase obligations of the Alabama
Law Enforcement Agency by an estimated $22,000 for information technology related
programming related to the offender's driving record.
Further, this bill revises the penalty for illegal use of a wireless telecommunications device from
$25, $50, and $75 for the first, second, and subsequent violations, respectively, under current
law, to: (1) $100 fine or 15-hours of community service and two points on the individual's
driving record for the first offense; (2) $200 fine or 30-hours of community service and two
points on the individual's driving record for the second offense within a 24-month period; and
(3) $300 fine or 45-hours of community service or both and three points on the individual's
driving record for the third or subsequent violations within a 24-month period.
This bill would also increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of Economic Affairs
(ADECA) by an undetermined amount to establish a hands-free communication device voucher
program; however, these obligations may be offset, wholly or in part, by the deposit of $25 of
each fine collected under this act into the Traffic Safety Trust Fund, administered by ADECA,
for operation of this program.
Further, this bill would require the Administrative Office of Courts (AOC) to establish and
maintain a database of all individuals charged with a violation of this act. According to AOC,
this bill will not increase its expenditures.

FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 8
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Representative Randy Wood
Security
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 03/22/2023
House Bill 8 as reported by the Committee on Public Safety and Homeland Security revises the
penalty for illegal use of a wireless telecommunications device from $25, $50, and $75 for the
first, second, and subsequent violations, respectively, under current law, to: (1) $100 fine or
15-hours of community service for the first conviction within a 24-month period; (2) $200 fine
or 30-hours of community service for the second conviction within a 24-month period; and (3)
$300 fine or 45-hours of community service or both for the third or subsequent violations within
a 24-month period.
Finally, this bill also prohibits the imposition of court costs associated solely with a violation
under theses provisions which could reduce receipts to the State General Fund, county general
funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited.
